The h-bearing and contracted y-forms therefore belong to this long-vowel derivative rather than automatically to bare dakṣiṇa; local vowels, endings and loss of nasalization are qualified. Prakrit already supplies initial ḍ, although Bagheli e/u vowels still need local review.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11533 vāma gives Kumaoni bāyõ, Old Awadhi bāeṁ ‘on the left’, Hindi bāyā̃ and Oriya bāyā̃ ‘pertaining to the left’. These y-bearing forms fit loss of intervocalic m with variable nasalization and v→b; unmarked nasalization and local final vowels remain qualified. Retained-m bama/bāmā and the h-bearing behiya are not silently grouped here.
